Process equipment

Equipment that stays running, in plants that cannot stop

We design, build and service the heat exchangers, separators and process skids that sit in the middle of a refinery, a chemical works or a food plant — the ones where an unplanned shutdown costs more in a day than the equipment cost to install.

See the equipment range Talk to a service engineer

Seventy-six years of the same problem

Northwind was founded in 1948 to build shell-and-tube exchangers for the Teesside chemical works. The materials have changed and the instrumentation is unrecognisable, but the engineering question has not moved: how do you get heat, pressure and flow to do what you want, continuously, in a vessel that somebody has to open up and clean out on a Tuesday in February?

That question is why we still make our own tube bundles, why our service engineers carry the drawings for units built before they were born, and why we quote lead times we can actually hold.

What we build

  • Shell-and-tube and plate heat exchangers, to ASME VIII and PED, in carbon steel through to duplex and titanium.
  • Two- and three-phase separators, horizontal and vertical, with internals designed for the actual crude or feedstock rather than a catalogue average.
  • Skid-mounted process packages, built and wet-tested in our works before they ever reach site.
  • Pressure vessels, columns and reactors up to 42 tonnes.

What we service

Roughly two-thirds of our revenue is service on equipment already in the ground — ours and other people's. Retube, re-rate, inspection, turnaround support and emergency response, from four regional workshops.

The unit we replaced last spring had been in continuous service since 1991. The bundle we pulled out of it was still Northwind's original.
